Implementation approach: Preserve protocol files exactly: requirements.txt, Main.py, tests/test_main.py. Keep Main.py thin and headless, running a single deterministic demo step and exiting. Place reusable logic in a snake_case package brick_breaker with an acyclic import graph. Ownership: config.py owns GameConfig and imports no project modules. level.py and game.py literally import GameConfig via 'from .config import GameConfig'. level.py must not import game.py. game.py may import make_grid_level from level.py. Separate domain entities (ball, paddle, brick) from pure rules (collision) and orchestration (game). No GUI or external frameworks; tests exercise pure logic deterministically with discrete ticks and abstracted input (left/right/none). Only pytest is listed in requirements.txt. Target Python 3.10 and avoid 3.11+ APIs. The single protocol test verifies runtime wiring via Main.run_demo and covers representative rules: a brick hit increments score and brick removal; a bottom-out decrements lives and resets level.
Domain Decomposition: Runtime bootstrap with a one-step deterministic demo and no I/O loops
